svg.title: claudia — rotating an object: handle, Format menu, Rotate By popover
svg.desc: Shared design for creates, computes and composes: the rotate handle with its states, the angle read-out while dragging, the Format menu with Rotate entries and keys, the Rotate By popover, and the object's context menu.
svg.text: claudia — rotating an object, the same way in all three apps
For review before any code. One handle on the canvas, one submenu in Format, one popover, one context menu. Rotation is whole degrees clockwise, 0–359, about the object's centre (D177).
Appears with the other handles when you hold an object (D82): 30 px above the
top edge, whatever the angle. The circle you see is 19 px; its hit area is 32
pointer on it, or focused with Tab
Focus ring: ink with a white edge.
The object turns live on your screen only; others see the result when you let go
(D82). A chip beside the handle reads the angle. Shift snaps to 15°; near 0°,
Beside Describe Object…, the other thing you do to the object you hold. Greyed
with nothing selected, and for a viewer.
Title Case, one label and one key in every client (D321, D361). On a Mac, Ctrl is
Cmd and Alt is Option. The keys are the ones the three menus leave free: the two
next to M on a US keyboard turn left and right.
Opens beside the object, like Apply Style…, so the object stays in view; movable
like the other overlays. Everything previews on the canvas. Enter or Done sends
one command; Esc puts it back.
degree short of a full turn.
Right-click, or Shift+F10 on the object. The same entries, the same keys;
the extra ones are the app's own.
Edit Text and Release From Grid exist in creates only (an object in a sheet or
a text has no grid and no slot to snap to). Describe Object… is new in
Rotate handle: a circle with a turning arrow on a stem above the top edge. It
is the only new thing on the canvas; resize handles and the outline turn with
the object, so they stay on its own edges.
The stem is for reach: the handle never hides under the top-middle resize
The centre is the pivot. It is not drawn while idle, so the picture stays
The tooltip names the keys. Hover and focus look the same, so a keyboard user
gets what a mouse user gets.
The ghost is the angle before you grabbed it; the dashed arc is how far you
With Shift, ticks at every 15° appear around the object, the long ones at 45°.
Within 3° of upright it snaps by itself and the chip gains a tick. Hold Alt to
Format ▸ Rotate ▸ Rotate Right 90°, Rotate Left 90°, Rotate By…. Every entry
has a key, checked against all three menus.
The dial is the same turn as the handle, for people who like a number and a
Whole degrees only, because the model stores 0–359 (D177). −10 is shown and
Upright sets 0°; without it, getting back to straight is a guess.
The object's menu names the same entries.
History reads “Rotate object · Arrow 2 · 0° → 37°”: one entry per drag, one undo.
Rotating by key, the menu or the popover is one entry too.
